name: showcase-6-equivalence-large
title: v1↔v2 equivalence at scale: a large (16×16) baseline ensemble graded against vEcoli
question:
Is the v2ecoli wild-type baseline still "the same E. coli" as vEcoli (v1) when
measured at LARGE ensemble scale? This study applies the PR #134 behavioral
report-card approach (population_phenotype_basal in its v1↔v2 *equivalence*
reference mode) to a large multi-generation baseline ensemble — 16 seeds × 16
generations — and grades v2's emergent population phenotype against a matched
vEcoli 16×16 reference within tolerance. #134 exercised the same loop at 8×16
as a demo; this study scales it to a population large enough to tighten the
omics/flux equivalence axes and to read v2's multi-generation behavior (the
in-process sawtooth, #142) honestly against v1.

report.title: showcase-6 — v1↔v2 equivalence of the baseline phenotype at large (16×16) scale
report.evidence_quality: matched 16×16 v2 (256 cells) vs vEcoli (185 cells) ensembles + reference-driven typed-criteria report card (PR
report.objective:
Establish whether the v2ecoli wild-type baseline population phenotype is
equivalent (within tolerance) to vEcoli's at large ensemble scale. The
instrument is the population_phenotype_basal report card (PR #134) rendered
in its vs_vecoli equivalence mode: the SAME 21-axis / 5-group card
(Physiology · Composition · Ribosomes · Exchange fluxes · Gene expression),
graded against a matched vEcoli ("v1") ensemble rather than v2's self-pin.
Scale is 16 seeds × 16 generations (2× the seeds of the #134 8×16 demo),
burn-in generation_lower_bound=3.
report.setup:
Card kind: population phenotypes (emergent behaviors over a seeds × gens
ensemble; cell-level aggregation — time-mean within a cell, then population
stats across cells). Reference mode: v1↔v2 equivalence (vs vEcoli).

MEASURED (v2) side: v2ecoli.composites.ecoli_baseline.ecoli_baseline driven by the basal
stimulus config v2ecoli/configs/population_phenotype_basal_16x16.json
(16 seeds × 16 generations, single_daughters, burn-in 3), resumed from a
full-ParCa cache (out/cache_full, 51 TF conditions). Dispatched Ray-parallel
(run_seeds_parallel) on the Mac mini with the parquet store as authoritative
(the in-engine ParquetEmitter is a RAM trap — use the sidecar). The card is
regenerated over the existing sweep with `v2ecoli-analyze <sweep> --config
configs/population_phenotype_basal_16x16.json` (no re-sim).

REFERENCE (vEcoli / v1) side: a matched 16×16 vEcoli ensemble produced from
the vEcoli source ALREADY AVAILABLE WITHIN v2ecoli (the in-repo vEcoli /
comparison-harness machinery used by the other v1↔v2 comparison reports —
NOT an external SMS/vecoli-benchmarking checkout). The reference is pinned
with scripts/pin_vecoli_equivalence_reference.py, which reuses the self-pin
reference as the presentation/criterion template and swaps in v1's per-cell
distributions (it carries self-contained cross-implementation readers for
the two v1↔v2 emit-schema differences — vEcoli's cumulative `time` vs
`global_time`, and positional `bulk` vs paired `bulk__id`/`bulk__count`), so
the shared analysis_runner stays untouched. The v1 commit is stamped in the
reference's stimulus.blessed_model_ref.

RENDER: reports/population_phenotype_basal_report.py
--analysis out/ppb16_parallel/parquet/analysis.json
--reference docs/report_cards/population_phenotype_basal/vs_vecoli/vecoli_reference.json
--sweep-dir out/ppb16_parallel/parquet --gen-lb 3 --model-ref bd2123d2
--out-dir docs/report_cards/population_phenotype_basal/vs_vecoli/
→ report_card.{html,md} (regenerated at 16×16 for this study). Rendered WITH
vector extraction (not --no-vectors) so the gene-expression r2 + exchange-flux
axes are graded, not ungraded.

ACTUAL RUN: v2 dispatched via the NEW parallel-by-default multi-seed path
(run_workflow → run_seeds_parallel, one Ray worker per seed, ~6 concurrent on
the 12-core/64 GB mini), which cut wall-time from ~17 h (single-process
meta-composite, ~4 min/cell sequential) to ~3.6 h for the full 256-cell
ensemble. vEcoli ran its own Nextflow workflow (CovertLab/vEcoli @ b237873e)
from the sibling in-repo checkout.
report.result:
Card overall: MISMATCH (12 within_tol ✓ · 6 drift ≈ · 3 mismatch ✗ · 0
ungraded), over all 21 axes graded at 16×16. v2 measured side = 256/256
cells (16 seeds × 16 full generations); v1 reference = 185-cell matched
vEcoli ensemble (b237873e); burn-in gen_lb 3. Sim-health banner: 232/256 v2
generations divided cleanly, 24 hit the duration cap without dividing (the
expected v2 in-process sawtooth, #142 — flagged, not hidden).

By group (Δ = v2 vs v1; p = Welch; d = Cohen's d):
  • PHYSIOLOGY (4 ✓ / 2 ≈): doubling time Δ −2.2% ✓, cell mass −4.4% ✓, cell
    volume −4.4% ✓, replication completion +4.7% ✓; oriC −6.3% ≈ drift,
    replication initiation −7.2% ≈ drift.
  • COMPOSITION (3 ✓): protein/DW +3.3% ✓, RNA/DW −1.5% ✓, DNA/DW +1.0% ✓ —
    fully equivalent.
  • RIBOSOMES (2 ✓ / 2 ≈): active fraction +0.1% ✓, elongation rate +0.2% ✓;
    total ribosomes −5.8% ≈ drift, rRNA-init production −8.7% ≈ drift.
  • EXCHANGE FLUXES (3 ✓ / 1 ≈ / 2 ✗ — THE DIVERGENCE): overall flux
    fingerprint R² = 0.9989 ✓ (40 matched, 0 appeared/lost, 6 sub-floor),
    glucose −4.4% ✓, ammonium −2.4% ✓; but O₂ exchange Δ −40.4% ✗ mismatch
    and CO₂ exchange Δ −20.3% ✗ mismatch (acetate sentinel ≈ drift, near
    floor). This is the O₂/CO₂ respiration deficit filed as issue #143 —
    and it PERSISTS at 16×16.
  • GENE EXPRESSION (1 ≈ / 1 ✗): transcriptome (mRNA cistrons) R² = 0.9461 ✗
    (below the strict 0.99 band), proteome (monomers) R² = 0.9613 ≈ drift —
    highly correlated but short of the strict self-pin equivalence band.
report.interpretation:
The #134 8×16 equivalence picture HOLDS at the larger 16×16 scale: v2 is
behaviorally the same E. coli as v1 on physiology, biomass composition, and
ribosome content (12 axes within tolerance, 6 in minor drift), and the
overall exchange-flux fingerprint is essentially identical (R² = 0.9989). The
card's overall MISMATCH is driven entirely by the THREE known, reproducible
divergences — O₂ (−40%) and CO₂ (−20%) exchange and the transcriptome R²
(0.95, below the strict 0.99 band) — not by any new discrepancy. The larger
seed count tightened the statistics (sub-percent p-values, clean effect
sizes) without changing the qualitative verdict: the divergence is a
localized respiratory-metabolism signature (issue #143) plus a gene-
expression correlation that sits just under the strict equivalence band, both
consistent with the 8×16 reading (R² ≈ 0.93–0.94 then, 0.95–0.96 now). The
instrument behaves as designed at scale: the metabolic divergence is the
signal, surfaced via typed criteria and the exchange-flux significance floor,
while FBA jitter near zero is shown but held below the floor.
report.decision:
PARTIAL EQUIVALENCE at 16×16. v2ecoli reproduces vEcoli's wild-type baseline
phenotype on physiology / composition / ribosomes / overall flux fingerprint
within tolerance; the divergence is confined to respiratory exchange (O₂/CO₂,
issue #143) and a gene-expression correlation just below the strict band. The
behavioral report-card instrument (PR #134) is confirmed to scale from 8×16
to 16×16 as a v1↔v2 equivalence test, and the divergence it flags is stable,
localized, and already filed — no new bug. Next: the principled cross-impl
statistics (TOST + per-axis δ margins) would convert the strict-band
gene-expression "mismatch" into an explicit equivalence-margin verdict.

assumptions.text:
A matched 16×16 vEcoli reference can be generated from the in-repo vEcoli
source and pinned with pin_vecoli_equivalence_reference.py; v1 and v2 share
cistron/monomer/flux ordering exactly, so the omics/flux vectors align
positionally with no ID remapping (verified at 8×16 in #134).

The population_phenotype_basal report card (PR #134) grades the SAME 21
axes at 16×16 as at 8×16 — scale changes the population statistics, not the
axis definitions or criteria — so the equivalence verdict at large scale is
directly comparable to the #134 8×16 demo.

v2's single-process multi-generation lineage runner sawtooths (in-process
state accumulation → degrade → divide-fail → reset-from-cache; #142); at
16 generations the burn-in (generation_lower_bound=3) and the card's
stationarity flag / variance decomposition surface this honestly rather than
letting it corrupt the graded window.

tests.name: physiology-equivalent-to-vecoli
tests.question: Is v2's physiology group (doubling time, cell mass/volume, oriC, replication timing) equivalent to vEcoli within tolerance at 16×16?

measure.detail: Physiology axes graded by ttest (Welch, magnitude bands + p-guard) vs the matched vEcoli reference; group verdict = worst axis (4 within_tol / 2 drift → drift → PASS+caveat).

tests.name: composition-equivalent-to-vecoli
tests.question: Are v2's biomass mass fractions (protein / RNA / DNA) equivalent to vEcoli within tolerance at 16×16?

measure.detail: Composition axes graded by ttest vs the matched vEcoli reference; group verdict = worst axis (3/3 within_tol → PASS).

tests.name: ribosomes-equivalent-to-vecoli
tests.question: Are v2's ribosome axes (total, active fraction, elongation rate, production) equivalent to vEcoli within tolerance at 16×16?

measure.detail: Ribosome axes graded by ttest; v1's 30S/50S counts read via a positional-bulk index adapter. Group verdict = worst axis (2 within_tol / 2 drift → drift → PASS+caveat).

tests.name: exchange-fluxes-equivalent-to-vecoli
tests.question: Are v2's exchange fluxes equivalent to vEcoli at 16×16, or does the

measure.detail: Exchange-flux signed scatter + KPIs vs the matched vEcoli reference; near-floor exchanges held below a significance floor. Group verdict = worst axis (O₂/CO₂ mismatch → FAIL); overall fingerprint R²=0.9989. The #143 respiration divergence.

tests.name: gene-expression-correlates-vecoli
tests.question: Does v2's transcriptome/proteome correlate with vEcoli at 16×16 (and does the outlier-gene set stay coherent)?

measure.detail: Transcriptome + proteome graded by r2 over ensemble-mean count vectors; companion outlier-gene tables. Group verdict = worst axis: transcriptome R²=0.946 is below the strict 0.99 band → mismatch → FAIL (proteome R²=0.961 → drift). The strict-band threshold drives the FAIL; TOST + per-axis δ margins (see study open question) would express this as an equivalence-margin verdict instead.

resolved_uncertainties: The #134 8×16 equivalence picture HOLDS at 16×16: Physiology / Composition / Ribosomes within tolerance (12 axes ✓, 6 minor drift), the overall exchange-flux fingerprint near-identical (R²=0.9989), the exchange-flux metabolic divergence (O₂ -40%, CO₂ -20%) persisting (issue #143), and gene expression highly correlated but below the strict 0.99 band (transcriptome R²=0.946, proteome R²=0.961 vs ~0.93–0.94 at 8×16). The larger sample tightened the statistics without changing the qualitative verdict.

A matched 16×16 vEcoli reference IS feasible from the in-repo sibling vEcoli (CovertLab/vEcoli @ b237873e) via its own Nextflow workflow. It ran to its natural maximum of 185 cells (9/16 single-daughter lineages completed all 16 gens; 7 truncated at deterministic FBA metabolic dead-ends — 256 unreachable for this seed set). 185 cells is a large, valid reference (> the 128-cell 8×16 demo).

v2's single-process meta-composite is impractically slow for 16×16 (~4 min/cell sequential → ~17 h); the new parallel-by-default multi-seed path (run_seeds_parallel) cut it to ~3.6 h for the full 256-cell ensemble. v2 completed all 16/16 lineages (256 cells); 24/256 generations hit the duration cap without dividing (the #142 sawtooth), surfaced by the card's sim-health banner.
remaining_uncertainties: The gene-expression 'mismatch' is a strict-band artifact (R²=0.946 vs a 0.99 threshold inherited from the self-pin template). The principled cross-impl form — TOST + per-axis δ equivalence margins — would convert this into an explicit equivalence-margin verdict rather than a hard fail. Nice-to-have, not blocking.
Root cause of the O₂/CO₂ respiratory-exchange divergence (issue #143) is not resolved here — this study confirms it is stable and localized at scale, it does not explain it.
